text.p: NeoPath Inc Friday said a U.S. Food and Drug Administration panel made a recommendation not to approve the conmpany's submission for the use of the AutoPap System as a Primary Screener of Pap smear slides pending the completion of additional premarket studies.
The following is a copy of the company's statement.

REDMOND, Wash.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Sept. 27, 1996--NeoPath, Inc. (NASDAQ:NPTH) announced today that a U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) Hematology and Pathology Devices Advisory Panel made a recommendation not to approve at this time the supplement to the company's premarket approval (PMA) submission for the use of the AutoPap(R) System as a Primary Screener of Pap smear slides pending the completion of additional premarket studies.
The Advisory Panel's recommendation will be considered by the FDA in completing its review of the company's supplement application.

The Advisory Panel asked NeoPath to present additional, on-site data that use of the AutoPap System as a Primary Screener of microscopic images from Pap smear slides is superior to the current standard of review, i.e., by a cytotechnologist followed by quality control review.

"FDA approval of the company's AutoPap 300 QC System a year ago was an important defining event for NeoPath, and we look forward to continuing to build a base of customers on this product," said Alan C. Nelson, Ph.D., president and chief executive officer of NeoPath Inc.

"We intend to work vigilantly to answer all of the Panel's questions and resubmit this matter to the FDA's Division of Clinical Laboratory Devices. Moreover, we will continue to provide our existing customers with the high level of service to which they have become accustomed, and will move forward with our marketing of the AutoPap 300 QC System. We are very confident that we will be able to meet the Panel's requests for further data on the Primary Screener indication," Nelson said.

The AutoPap System utilizes proprietary image-processing computers to identify those pap smears with the highest potential for abnormality. The image-interpretation technology of the AutoPap System consists of integrated high-speed microscopes, specialized image interpretation software and field-of-view computers. This technology allows for rapid acquisition, analysis and classification of information contained within complex, highly variable images such as those that occur in the cellular material of a Pap smear. Based on those images, the system automatically analyzes and extracts important features of cellular material and classifies specimens.

NeoPath's PMA supplement was accepted for filing on June 6, 1996. The original PMA application for the AutoPap System to be used for quality control rescreening was submitted to the FDA on Feb. 24, 1995, and approved on Sept. 29, 1995. The U.S. Health Care Financing Administration (HCFA) approved use of the device as a replacement for traditional methods of quality control rescreening in March of 1996.

NeoPath, Inc.'s core expertise is in the research, development, and commercialization of technologies to automate the interpretation of medical images. The company, which is based in Redmond, has approximately 175 employees. -0-
